title: Ticket surge thresholds and rollout readiness huddle
summary: Internal planning huddle to finalize thresholds and operational playbook for an upcoming model rollout. Agreed on three tiered ticket surge thresholds, adjusted alert windows, and a staged canary with automatic fallback. Action items assigned for docs, runbook tests, and a post-rollout simulation.
competitors_mentioned: internal comparison with previous GCU runbooks
next_steps: Ben to run a canary dry-run in staging and post results in #deployments by 2026-02-09
Priya to update pager thresholds and create a muted alert for P90 token latency by 2026-02-07
Jonah to schedule capacity stress test for dedicated pools on 2026-02-08
Alex to circulate final rollout timetable and send invites for the tabletop on 2026-02-10
action_items: Ben Chu | run canary dry-run and collect telemetry | due: 2026-02-09
Priya Shah | update alert rules and add muted P90 alert | due: 2026-02-07
Jonah Lee | run capacity stress test across 3 regions | due: 2026-02-08
Lydia Park | prepare QA checklist for rollback verification | due: 2026-02-09
Alex Moreno | publish final timetable and tabletop agenda | due: 2026-02-06
transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-02-05; Start: 15:00 PST; Duration approx 65 minutes; Attendees listed.

[00:00] Alex Moreno: Alright, uh, thanks everyone for joining. Quick check — we only have an hour, um, but we need to lock thresholds and the playbook for the rollout next week.
[00:22] Priya Shah: Yep, I'll be brief. We ran the alerting sims last night — remember a couple of things: our current P95 latency alert fires at 750ms which is too noisy for the new model, and the token backpressure manifests at the request proxy level first.
[00:39] Jonah Lee: Right, and we saw the proxy queue spike at about 1.6x baseline at the 300 concurrent request mark in staging. The dedciated pool will absorb some but if we hit 2.5x we risk KV cache misses that amplify latency.
[00:57] Maya Ortiz: (interruption) When you say KV cache misses, do you mean the prefix cache? We had a different profile for the smaller model.
[01:10] Jonah Lee: Yeah prefix K V cache — sorry, transcription note, prefix cache misses. That increases token compute by about 12-18% on average for long prompts.
[01:25] Alex Moreno: OK so threshold tiering proposition: green under 1.5x, amber 1.5x-2.2x, red >2.2x. Green is normal ops; amber triggers canary throttles and increased batching; red triggers fallback to smaller quantized model variants and capacity surge. Thoughts?
[01:48] Priya Shah: I like it but change amber upper bound to 2.0 not 2.2 — leaves a buffer for network variance. Also amber should mute customer-facing alerts and only page the on-call with a low-priority flag.
[02:06] Ben Chu: Agree on mute. For canary throttles — do we mean increasing per-tenant concurrency caps or lowering token max? Because per-tenant cap changes need client-side coordination.
[02:24] Maya Ortiz: Lowering token max seems safer. We can ship a soft-limit that returns a structured hint to the client to shorten context.
[02:34] Hannah Ruiz: From support POV, we need the hint wording in the playbook so agents can triage user tickets quickly. Also please cc us on the canary results.
[02:47] Samir Khatri: On timelines — what's the exact canary window? I thought earlier plan was 4 hours in staging then 2 hours in prod canary?
[03:02] Alex Moreno: Revised plan: 2 hours in staging with synthetic traffic at 1.2x expected, then a 3-hour prod canary with 1% traffic ramp to 20% using the new rollout-controller and auto-fallback enabled.
[03:18] Jonah Lee: Auto-fallback needs the routing table update — I'll push the change to make fallback route to quantized-xt0 then to quantized-xt1 variants. We should also make sure dedciated pool autoscale is allowed to spike 30% for the window.
[03:36] Priya Shah: Autoscale spike is okay but add a safety cap — no more than 50% of reserved capacity to avoid affecting other tenants. And add a throttling policy where if tail latency P99 climbs >1s for 2 consecutive minutes we force fallback.
[03:55] Ben Chu: Two things: add a fast rollback (0min) toggle and a staged rollback (drip) in case of partial regressions. Also we need a test proving rollback actually reduces error rate within 3 minutes.
[04:12] Lydia Park: QA will run the rollback verification checklist. We'll simulate KV cache miss scenarios and ensure the small model returns compatible Json schema for client parsers.
[04:26] Priya Shah: Note: schema drift was the cause of last month's regression — the smaller model had an extra top-level field and some clients broke. Add schema asserts to the canary check.
[04:40] Alex Moreno: Good call. Action: add schema asserts to canary gating.
[04:45] (crosstalk)
[04:52] Jonah Lee: On alert noise reduction — we propose a short hold window: only escalate if amber persists for 5 minutes and red persists for 60s, otherwise treat as transient. This reduces flapping.
[05:09] Priya Shah: Agree, 5m amber hold, 60s red hold. Also implement a cooldown period of 10m before re-escalating for same tenant.
[05:21] Maya Ortiz: How are we classifying tiered traffic? By route, model, customer plan? Need to be explicit so support knows who to contact.
[05:34] Alex Moreno: For this rollout we use route-level tags: /generate/long-context is high-risk, /chat is moderate. Also we include a per-customer override for enterprise tenants.
[05:46] Hannah Ruiz: Please add a mapping doc for us, we'll put it into the triage playbook.
[05:52] Ben Chu: Small but important: benchmarked latency delta for quantized variant is about +30ms median but 0.2x cost, so cost tradeoff is enormous. We should be explicit in the playbook about cost vs latency targets.
[06:12] Alex Moreno: Noted. Everyone, remember the revenue impact on customers if we over-quantize.
[06:20] Priya Shah: One more incident-specific note — audit logs during last rollout were incomplete because of missing KMS key rotation metadata. We need to verify KMS headers are passed through the private control plane.
[06:35] Jonah Lee: I'll run a quick KMS header end-to-end test during staging run.
[06:40] Alex Moreno: Good. Okay, let's run through the actual playbook steps, I'm going to read the checklist and you call out if anything missing. Step 1: notify SRE and Release Slack channel, Step 2: set canary timers and synthetic load, Step 3: enable auto-fallback policy, Step 4: monitor telemetry and schema asserts, Step 5: run rollback if any gating fails.
[07:05] Priya Shah: Under Step 1 add: notify Support and Account execs for affected enterprise tenants.
[07:12] Lydia Park: Under Step 4 add: run QA schema verifier and tokenization parity check.
[07:20] Ben Chu: Under Step 3 add: a manual override endpoint if auto-fallback misroutes.
[07:29] Alex Moreno: Manual override noted. Next: telemetry — what dashboards should be green? Priya?
[07:35] Priya Shah: Dashboards: token throughput, proxy queue length, prefix cache hit rate, per-tenant P95/P99, and error rate by route. Make sure we have a combined rollup dashboard for a quick at-a-glance.
[07:50] Jonah Lee: I'll create the rollup and link it in the playbook. It will include a small latency heatmap.
[07:58] Maya Ortiz: Also add a synthetic end-to-end user journey check — not just API-level, but client UI render timing to catch regressions.
[08:10] Hannah Ruiz: That helps support too.
[08:15] (brief pause, background typing)
[08:28] Alex Moreno: Ok let's talk about runbook language and Support scripts — Hannah, can you draft the agent script for the amber and red scenarios?
[08:36] Hannah Ruiz: Yes, I'll draft two short scripts: one for amber (informational, offer workaround hint) and one for red (escalate to engineering, create escalation ticket).
[08:46] Lydia Park: We'll add reproducible steps for QA and a short checklist for rollback verification.
[08:52] Ben Chu: One more ops-run thought — we should simulate a cache warmup failure where we intentionally flush the prefix cache and ensure fallback still recovers under 5 minutes.
[09:05] Priya Shah: Good test. Schedule it in the stress test.
[09:10] Alex Moreno: Timeline recap: 2026-02-07 update alert rules; 2026-02-08 capacity stress tests; 2026-02-09 canary dry-run in staging; 2026-02-10 tabletop and final go/no-go. Anything blocking?
[09:28] Jonah Lee: Need a quick infra change to allow autoscale spike for dedicated pools — I'll open the infra PR today.
[09:35] Priya Shah: I need the PR link before I can update alerts, otherwise I'll update the SLO pages with tentative numbers.
[09:42] Alex Moreno: We'll wait a day for the PR review; priya, update the alerts tentatively and finalize when PR lands.
[09:49] (background chatter)
[10:02] Ben Chu: Small note about telemetry retention — we'll increase short-term retention for related metrics to 30 days for postmortem analysis. Jonah will that impact storage?
[10:12] Jonah Lee: It will, but it's manageable if we limit to the rollup dashboard's metric set. I'll scope it in the PR.
[10:21] Maya Ortiz: Another risk: client-side rate limiting. Some clients will hit 429s during canary and we need a standard message. Add that to the support scripts.
[10:33] Hannah Ruiz: We'll craft the message — include next_steps and link to status page.
[10:40] Alex Moreno: Ok we're close. Final quick round: any blockers from legal/security?
[10:47] Priya Shah: Security asked for an audit-run of the private control plane keys — they want the run completed before the prod canary. We can do it on 2026-02-08 as well.
[10:58] Alex Moreno: Great. Last thing — post-rollout simulation: we'll run a 1-week smoke and then an expanded regression check at 72 hours. Lydia, prepare the regression harness.
[11:10] Lydia Park: On it.
[11:14] Alex Moreno: Thanks everyone, I'll send out the updated timetable. Recap of owners — Ben runs canary, Priya updates alerts, Jonah infra tests and PR, Lydia QA, Hannah support scripts, Alex publishes agenda. Meeting adjourned.

End of transcript.
